 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.776/2016 dated 05.07.2017 on the file of the XXI ACMM & XXIII Addl.
Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Bengaluru.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in the accident.
The claimants are husband and son of the deceased.

The case of the claimant is that on 17.01.2016 at about 4.45 p.m. the deceased-Rajamma was traveling in an auto from Sathnoor to Kanakapura Taluk, at that the driver of the auto drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the lorry which is parked in the middle of the road by its driver without giving any signal.
Because of it, the deceased had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the death on spot.

According to the claimants, she was doing embroidery work and Siddaraju vs Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49968544/
2 earning an amount of Rs.15,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Her husband and son are dependents on her, as both of them are handicapped.

The court below has come to the conclusion that there is a rash and negligent driving on the part both the driver of the auto as well as there is negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and apportioned the negligence at 75% and 25% on both the vehicles.
When it comes to the liability, driver of the NC: 2023:KHC:40769 auto was not having a valid driving license and there is no permit to drive the vehicle.
The court below had exonerated the insurance company who has insured the Auto and held that the owner alone is liable to pay the compensation.
When it comes to the compensation, the court below had given a finding that they are not the dependents and they are not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of dependency.

They cannot be termed as dependents and they are only entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of estate but not loss of dependency and granted an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- under the head of loss of estate.
Under the head of consortium granted an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- and an amount of Rs.25,000/- was granted towards transport and funeral expenses.
Towards loss of love and affection an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- was granted.

Altogether a compensation of an amount of Rs.3,75,000/-
was granted by the Tribunal.
Learned counsel for the claimant submits that deceased was doing embroidery work and earning an amount of Rs.15,000/- and both the claimants are handicapped and depending on her.
The court below had failed to consider the same, under head of loss of dependency failed to grant any amounts.
It is submitted that the compensation that was awarded was not just and reasonable.

It is further submitted that when the permit is not there and there was no license to the driver of Auto, it is a contract between the insured and insurer and the deceased being a third party, the court ought to have applied the principle of pay and recovery.
It is submitted that the Tribunal had failed to consider any of these aspects and granted a very meager compensation by exonerating the insurer of the Auto.

4. Learned counsel for the insurance company, which insured the Auto submits that the Tribunal had rightly exonerated the insurance company as there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy, where there NC: 2023:KHC:40769 is no permit and no driving license to the driver of the vehicle.
Learned counsel for the insurance company which insured the lorry submits that the Tribunal had rightly not granted any compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
Neither husband nor the son are dependents upon the deceased and no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the entire material on record.
In this case, according to the claimants, they are handicapped and the deceased was doing embroidery work and earning amounts and contributing the same to the family.
The court below had taken an amount of Rs.8,000/- as income but however had not granted any amount under the head of loss of dependency.
Considering the fact that these two claimants are handicapped and considering them as dependents, this court is inclined to grant the compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
As this is an accident of the year 2016, this court is inclined NC: 2023:KHC:40769 to consider the income at an amount of Rs.9,500/-.

Without there being any evidence, the deceased was 48 years Siddaraju vs Reliance General Insurance Co Ltd on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49968544/
3 old, 25% future prospects would come to an amount of Rs.2,375/-, it would be an amount of Rs.11,875/-.

an amount of Rs.3,958/-.
Her contribution to the family would come to Rs.7,917/- x 12 x Multiplier 13 comes to an amount of Rs.12,35,052/-.
Both the husband and son are the claimants, towards consortium Rs.44,000/- x 2 =Rs.88,000/- is granted.
Towards funeral expenses an amount of Rs.33,000/- is granted.

6. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V. MEKALA -vs- M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER 1, the claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.

Then coming to the negligence, it was apportioned at 75% on the driver of Lorry and 25% on the Auto.
The insurer of the Auto was exonerated as there are violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the Appellant, the deceased is a third party to the insurance, even if there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy,
still the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

In view of the same, this court holds that insurer NC:
2023:KHC:40769 of the Auto is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

This court has arrived at compensation of an amount of Rs.13,66,052/-
as the insurer of the lorry i.e., Respondent No.1-Insurance Company is liable to pay an amount of Rs.10,24,539/-.
The insurer of the Auto i.e, Respondent No.2 is liable to pay an amount of Rs.3,41,513/-.
